review_candidates.title: Team Leader
review_candidates.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised. Please note this is an evergreen position. We accept applications on an ongoing basis to build a talent pipeline for roles that open regularly. Because this posting may not reflect a current opening, we may not contact every applicant. If your background aligns with an open need, our team will reach out. We also encourage you to visit our careers page to explore other opportunities. BACKGROUND: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The IRC leads the way from harm to home. The IRC responds to people’s acute and longer-term needs with integrated programs that improve health and safety, prioritize children’s education, foster economic wellbeing, and empower communities to regain control over their lives. Our work gives rise to some of the most pressing issues facing contemporary humanitarian action, including questions of access, conflict sensitivity, coordination, and impact. The International Rescue Committee (IRC) have been working in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) for more than forty years. Today, the IRC has more than 2,200 staff working across the region, including in Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, and Yemen to support those affected by some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises. The IRC Yemen began its programs in October 2012. Since establishing its presence in the South of Yemen, in the Red Sea Coastal city of Aden, following the war which broke out in Yemen in March of 2015 and the humanitarian disaster. IRC launched an emergency response program to support conflict-affected and displaced communities, with programmes in Health, Nutrition, Protection (including Women’s Protection and Empowerment and Child Protection), emergency preparedness and response Mechanisms and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH). IRC Yemen currently implements the FCDO-funded RISE Consortium (a health and protection programme) in southern Yemen together with national partner organisations Background and Objectives of YHC Yemen continues to face one of the world’s most severe humanitarian crises, driven by years of conflict, economic disruption and the degradation of public services. Only 54% of health facilities are currently functioning, and just 18% of those offer at least 75% service availability. Maternal mortality stands at 183 per 100,000 live births and under-five mortality at 61.9 per 1,000. Food security and basic needs are the top priority for 80% of households; 96% of households are food insecure, and 47% report insufficient water to meet their daily needs. Intimate partner and household-based gender-based violence predominates, while services are constrained by a severe shortage of female caseworkers and fragmented referral pathways. The Yemen Humanitarian Capacity programme is an anticipated FCDO-funded, three-year programme expected to succeed the current RISE programme. YHC is designed to deliver lifesaving, integrated health, nutrition, and protection services across Yemen. Job Summary The Team Leader provides overall strategic leadership, accountability and representation for the YHC programme. They are accountable to FCDO and to IRC for delivering programme results, quality, compliance and value for money. The Team Leader is IRC’s senior representative to FCDO, consortium partners and national and international stakeholders on YHC, and line-manages the YHC senior management team. Major Responsibilities Strategic Leadership and Programme Delivery Provide overall strategic direction for YHC, ensuring delivery against the FCDO agreement, logframe, workplan and budget, and alignment with FCDO priorities, IRC standards and humanitarian principles. Ensure integration across health, nutrition and protection (and any other sectors in the final scope), with a concentrated focus on core health system functions and service quality. Lead adaptive management and contingency planning so that the programme remains resilient to access, funding and operating-environment shocks, including the loss of access to specific areas or delivery channels. Consortium Governance, Partnerships and Localisation Establish and chair consortium governance structures with meaningful partner representation and decision-making authority, including joint planning, review and learning processes. Ensure common reporting, supervision approaches, tools and quality standards are agreed across partners before implementation begins, rather than aligned after the fact. Manage consortium relationships and resolve partnership issues constructively, ensuring equitable, accountable and transparent partnerships. Donor Relations and Representation Serve as the senior point of contact for FCDO Yemen on programme strategy, performance, risk and funding, maintaining a proactive, transparent and solutions-oriented relationship. Represent IRC and YHC in humanitarian and development coordination fora, including cluster and sector platforms, donor groups and NGO coordination bodies. Proactively communicate programme risks, mitigation measures and adaptive management decisions to FCDO in line with the programme’s risk management framework. Identify and communicate emerging evidence, learning and policy-relevant findings from YHC, contributing to donor and sector dialogue on localisation, value for money and health systems strengthening. Risk, Compliance and Remote Management Establish and maintain a consortium risk management framework covering programmatic, security, fiduciary, reputational, sanctions, counter-terrorism and diversion risks, with regular review and clear escalation. Comply with FCDO, UK and IRC legal, sanctions and compliance requirements, working closely with IRC Legal and Compliance. Ensure appropriate remote management, supervision, monitoring and verification arrangements, including third-party monitoring where needed, to provide FCDO and IRC with assurance over delivery.. Uphold humanitarian principles, do-no-harm, safeguarding and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) across the consortium, ensuring incidents are reported and managed in line with IRC and FCDO requirements. Ensure audit readiness and coordinate with internal audit, compliance and regional teams throughout the programme cycle. Financial Stewardship and Value for Money Hold overall accountability for the YHC budget, ensuring expenditure is on track, compliant with FCDO financial management requirements and aligned to approved workplans, working closely with Finance and consortium partners. Ensure sub-award management, procurement and operational processes meet IRC and FCDO standards, including anti-fraud, anti-corruption and conflict-of-interest requirements. Lead the integration of FCDO’s value-for-money framework into programme planning, implementation and reporting, and contribute to FCDO comparisons of cost efficiency across approaches, ensuring costs, including systems-strengthening and capacity-development investment, are classified consistently. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Ensure data quality assurance, data protection and ethical standards are applied consistently across partners, including remote and third-party monitoring where required. Champion accountability to affected populations (AAP), including accessible feedback and complaint mechanisms, and ensure findings are used to improve programme delivery. Promote a culture of learning and adaptive management, including after-action reviews, lessons-learned exercises and pause-and-reflect sessions. Team Leadership and Management Lead, line-manage and develop the YHC senior management team, providing mentoring and performance support. Ensure the YHC staffing plan is recruited and retained, with clear roles across IRC and consortium partners. Foster a culture of collaboration, learning, inclusion and continuous improvement, and promote staff care, safety and security. Coordinate closely with the Country Director, Deputy Director of Programmes, operations and support functions, and regional and global teams to ensure YHC is fully supported and aligned with the IRC Yemen country strategy. Education QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS Master’s degree in international development, public health, humanitarian affairs, public policy, social sciences, or a related field. Equivalent professional experience may be considered. Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in complex humanitarian and/or development programming, with at least 5 years in senior leadership of large, multi-year, multi-partner programmes. Demonstrated experience leading large-scale, multi-sector FCDO-funded programmes (or equivalent bilateral donors), including responsibility for results, compliance, budgets and donor relationships. Proven experience leading consortia, including working with national and local NGOs and advancing localisation agendas. Substantial experience in conflict-affected and access-constrained contexts, including remote management of delivery through partners and third-party monitoring. Strong understanding of donor compliance, due diligence, sanctions and counter-terrorism requirements, and risk management in complex operating environments Technical grounding in at least two of the following: health systems strengthening, nutrition, protection (including GBV and child protection), or food security and livelihoods. Experience in applying value-for-money frameworks in programme management and donor reporting. WORKING ENVIRONMENT The position is based in Yemen with expected travel to programme and partner locations as security and access permit, and to regional and headquarters offices. Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients. Memahami penerapan K3 kelistrikan, pengendalian mutu, manajemen risiko, dan administrasi perubahan pekerjaan. Bersedia melakukan perjalanan dinas, penugasan ke site, serta mengelola beberapa proyek sesuai kebutuhan perusahaan.
